title: CASE OF A.P. v. SLOVAKIA
conclusion: Violation of Article 3 - Prohibition of torture (Article 3 - Degrading treatment) (Substantive aspect);Violation of Article 3 - Prohibition of torture (Article 3 - Effective investigation) (Procedural aspect)
summary: In the case of A.P. v. Slovakia, the applicant, A.P., is a young man of Roma origin living in Rudňany, Slovakia. The case highlights the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers, who often face police violence and inadequate protection from state authorities. On 11 February 2015, when A.P. was 16 years old, he was identified by another Roma boy as a possible attacker in a minor incident. Municipal police officers confronted A.P. in front of his school, where he alleged that he was grabbed, punched in the face, and then further assaulted at the police station, all while being pressured to confess. Medical records from the same day confirmed injuries consistent with his account. Despite his complaints, the initial police investigation was superficial, relying mainly on the officers’ testimonies and failing to consider independent witnesses or the possibility of racial motivation. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which prohibits torture and inhuman or degrading treatment. The Court found both a substantive violation, due to the ill-treatment by police, and a procedural violation, due to the ineffective investigation. This judgment is significant as it reinforces the obligation of states to protect Roma and Travellers from police abuse and to ensure thorough investigations, reflecting ongoing concerns about anti-Roma violence and discrimination in Europe.
